stimulus.source_note: Florentine Codex, Book 12, c. 1585, public domain, Wikimedia Commons. Image viewed before writing.
stimulus.text: This drawing from the Florentine Codex, Book 12, shows Nahua people suffering from smallpox in central Mexico in the 1500s. On the left, a sick person covered in spots lies on a mat while another person leans over them. On the right, bodies covered in spots lie still on woven mats, unable to move.

stem: This drawing from the Florentine Codex shows Nahua people suffering from smallpox in central Mexico in the 1500s. What does the image show about the epidemic?

options.text: Smallpox was brought to the Americas deliberately, as a Spanish weapon of war.
options.misconception: The image shows victims of an epidemic, not a deliberate attack; the disease spread through contact, and no source shows the Spanish spreading it on purpose in this period.

options.text: The disease struck whole households at once, leaving the sick unable to move.
Smallpox arrived in the Americas from Africa with enslaved laborers.
options.misconception: Smallpox came from Europe with the colonists; the large-scale African slave trade grew later and did not bring the first epidemics.

options.text: Native peoples had immunity to smallpox from earlier exposure to the disease.
options.misconception: The victims are covered in sores and lying helpless; the image shows a people with no immunity at all.

instruction: Answer from the stimulus and stem only. Pick one option. Do not open the question file.
